title: Would people be interested in "How to make puzzles for MZ" guides?

posts.author: VilNess
posts.body:
Hi all!
My biggest enjoyment regarding game developing is currently puzzle & level planning. Now, after about 3 years of using MZ for games that are mostly puzzle based, I do honestly feel I could have a lot to give to RPG maker community.
Most of my built puzzles are in a slippery environment  and I use a lot of the Visustella Events move core -plugin, since it has
lots of great features. One of my favourite is the "Move Down Until Stop" function (or Up, Left, Right) which saves a lot
of time in many situations.
Also, what I have often in my game is a "pathchecker" event that checks the distance of tiles to a specific region ID before the player moves. This enables me to have the main character (for example) slide over certain ground if the distance is big enough.
This path checker teleports to players location when a direction input is made, then it starts moving in the players direction. Every tile it proceeds, it adds 1 to the distance variable. As long as it is moving in a neutral region ID, the distance grows. Once
the path checker hits a non-neutral region ID, it stops and the distance variable value can have conditions. For example, if the value is 2 or less the player moves 2 tiles with certain sprites but if the value is 3 or more the player may have different sprites.
Also, after certain value the path checker can keep on moving in certain region IDs (like semi slippery floor) so that if the player has a distance of 4 or more to a semineutral ground, it doesn´t stop the player and instead it keeps on moving.
This might be hard to understand but if you try my Icekai game, I´m sure you´ll quickly understand what I mean.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body:
"How to design puzzles" absolutely sounds like an extremely useful thing to have because so many different creators would want it... and would likely be long enough to release as a
novel
. "How to implement a puzzle idea into MZ" is also very useful and would likely be a practical breakdown of eventing. I separate those because they are very different tutorials and it's a good idea to figure out which one you want to make.
